about: Read-quality challenge set for the Social Receipt engine (path to 9.0, step 2). Each case is a realistic draft run through buildReceipt with the stated context. fit/fitWhy are human judgments authored after seeing the engine output: fits = verdict, suggested message and best move agree with what the draft means; borderline = defensible but strained; misfit = the read contradicts the draft's plain meaning. Engine output lives in tests/challenge-results.json, regenerated by tests/run-challenge-set.js.

cases.draft: I love you and I want to help, but I can't lend you money this month. I have to protect my own bills first. It's not personal.
cases.fitWhy: The verdict is fair, the draft IS a good message, but bestMove 'Reply and move forward' and the stock suggested line ignore the boundary entirely; the receipt's advice surface never engages with what the draft says.
cases.intent: Healthy boundary: warm, firm, kind. Should NOT read as hostile or as a problem; 'this works' is an acceptable read.

cases.draft: Please don't call after 10pm unless it's an emergency. I need my sleep before work and I'm not able to chat late anymore.
cases.fitWhy: PARTIALLY FIXED: the sales hijack is gone (bare 'call' no longer marks a draft as a sales motion), so the receipt is no longer a sales close. The headline still misfits: 'You're over-investing. They're not matching you.' for a sleep boundary, because 'i need' in the highIntent lexicon cannot distinguish needing sleep from needing reassurance. No gate-safe fix: the difference is the object of the need, which substring matching cannot see; it needs object-aware parsing (need + reassurance object vs need + concrete object).
cases.intent: Healthy boundary: a sleep/phone limit stated plainly. Should NOT be read as over-investing in an unmatched relationship or as conflict.

cases.draft: I'm not able to cover your shift on Saturday. I hope you find someone who can.
cases.fitWhy: Professional read, sensible move and timing. Confidence 3 is the gauge honestly reporting almost no matched signals, and its basis is disclosed in the app.
cases.intent: Healthy boundary at work: a clean decline. A professional, neutral read fits.

cases.draft: You're a selfish jerk and I'm sick of your crap. Don't ever text me again.
cases.fitWhy: FIXED: 'jerk' now trips the conflict flag, so the receipt is coherent: activated verdict, Create space, High risk, calm suggested line.
cases.intent: Genuine aggression: name-calling and a cutoff. Should read as hostile/high-risk, NOT as a neutral 'next move matters' shrug.

cases.draft: Shut up. You always ruin everything and nobody actually likes you, we just tolerate you.
cases.fitWhy: FIXED: 'shut up' now trips the conflict flag; the spine itself produces the activated verdict with Create space and High risk instead of borrowing a pattern label with generic fields.
cases.intent: Genuine aggression: contempt and social exclusion. Should read as hostile, NOT neutral.

cases.draft: You never listen to a single word I say and you only care about yourself.
cases.fitWhy: Activated verdict, Create space, High risk, calm suggested line: verdict, move and suggestion all agree with the draft's meaning.
cases.intent: Control: aggression phrased with the engine's known trigger wording. An activated/conflict read fits.

cases.draft: Sorry. Sorry, sorry. I know I keep saying it but I feel awful and I need you to tell me we are good because I cannot stop thinking about it. Please forgive me.
cases.fitWhy: FIXED: new verdict branch (apology + highIntent, ahead of the positive branch) returns 'One apology lands. The rest is asking for reassurance.', which finally agrees with the same receipt's bestMove ('Wait') and risk (Medium-High). The scripts page's embedded copy of this receipt was updated in the same change, so the public page no longer teaches with the misfit read.
cases.intent: THE known audit case, verbatim: a distressed, reassurance-seeking apology. It must NOT be read as 'This is working'; the user is spiraling and asking the other person to soothe them.

cases.draft: I was wrong to raise my voice at dinner last night. That was on me, no excuses. I'm sorry.
cases.fitWhy: IMPROVED: the dating suggested line is gone (a lexical romantic flag no longer overrides an explicit Friend / Family scenario). The suggested message is now neutral stock filler, still not apology-aware, so the case stays borderline rather than fits.
cases.intent: Clean accountability: owns a specific act, no excuses, no ask. A calm, lands-well read fits.

cases.draft: I messed up the reservation and we lost the table. My fault entirely. I've already rebooked for Friday at 7 and I'll cover the deposit.
cases.fitWhy: A model apology with repair already completed gets the generic default verdict and 'Clarify the goal'. Nothing recognizes the accountability or the finished repair. Not hostile, just empty, and its 'dont' line is written for the apology's receiver, not its sender.
cases.intent: Accountability plus concrete repair already done. Should read as a strong, settled apology, not distress.

cases.draft: Please tell me you're not mad. Sorry, sorry, sorry, I keep thinking about it and I can't sleep. Just tell me we're fine, please forgive me.
cases.fitWhy: Directionally humane ('needed space', Wait, Medium-High), but damning next to b1: same psychology, opposite headline, decided only by the incidental words 'mad' (conflict) vs 'good' (positive). The pattern layer even saw 'Reassurance-seeking cue' here while the spine's verdict ignored the same signal in b1.
cases.intent: Same psychology as b1 (repeated sorry, cannot sleep, begging for 'we're fine') phrased slightly differently. Consistency check against b1: two drafts this alike should not receive opposite verdicts.

cases.draft: I'm sorry I forgot your birthday. I feel awful about it. Can I take you to dinner this week to make it up to you?
cases.fitWhy: IMPROVED: same fix as b2; the birthday apology no longer ships a dating line as its suggestion. Suggestion remains generic.
cases.intent: Mild, proportionate apology with a repair offer. Verdict, suggested message and best move should all be about the apology, not about dating signals.

cases.draft: You told me I never listen and honestly that hurt to hear. Can we talk about it tonight?
cases.fitWhy: The user quotes the other person's accusation, says it hurt, and asks to talk. The verdict 'You almost overplayed it', High risk and 'Create space' blame the reporter for words they explicitly attributed to someone else.
cases.intent: The user QUOTES the other person's accusation and says it hurt. The read should not blame the user for 'overplaying' an accusation they did not make.

cases.draft: When you said 'you only care about yourself' earlier, it stung. I don't think that's fair, but I want to hear you out.
cases.fitWhy: Same failure with explicit quote marks around the accusation: the pattern layer even names the quoted phrase as the user's own 'Broad claim about caring'. Quotation is invisible to substring matching.
cases.intent: Quoted accusation in explicit quote marks, user responding with restraint. Same expectation as c1.

cases.draft: You never listen to me, and you only care about yourself. I'm tired of it.
cases.fitWhy: Control behaves: when the user actually makes the accusation, the activated verdict, Create space and High risk are the right read.
cases.intent: Control: the user MAKES the accusation. An activated/conflict read fits here.

cases.draft: You said I'm always the problem in this relationship. I don't agree, but I want to understand why you see it that way.
cases.fitWhy: IMPROVED in part: the dating suggested line and Low-risk dating framing are gone. The verdict still attributes the quoted words to the user as self-blame; the attribution problem itself is unfixed (see family c diagnosis).
cases.intent: Same move as c1/c2 (reporting the other's words, calmly) but without the engine's trigger phrases. Consistency check: the read should be roughly as fair as c1/c2's ought to be.

cases.draft: Sounds good, thanks!
cases.fitWhy: Warm read, forward move, low risk: correct.
cases.intent: Short warm reply. Should read as warm/working, NOT cold or low-investment.

cases.draft: ok sounds good
cases.fitWhy: 'ok' does not drag it into the not-invested read; the positive wording wins, correctly.
cases.intent: Casual warm agreement. The 'ok' must not drag it into the one-word 'not invested' read when 'sounds good' is right there.

cases.draft: Thank you so much, that honestly made my day. You're the best!
cases.fitWhy: FIXED from misfit: 'made' no longer trips the conflict flag ('mad' is now matched in bounded forms), so gratitude is no longer read as a conflict needing space at High risk. What remains is a coverage gap: no positive lexicon entry fires on 'made my day' or 'the best', so the verdict is the generic default at low confidence. A shrug, but an honest one.
cases.intent: Unmistakable warmth and gratitude. Should read as warm/positive, not as an unreadable generic draft.

cases.draft: That works for me. I was thinking we could also invite Ana, she missed the last one and keeps asking about it, plus she makes everything more fun.
cases.fitWhy: IMPROVED: 'works' no longer trips the professional flag ('work' is now matched in bounded forms), so a plan with friends no longer gets a workplace follow-up and business-hours timing. The verdict remains the generic default; the warmth/engagement lexicon simply has no entry for this kind of substance.
cases.intent: Engaged reply with real substance and initiative. Should not read as cold, anxious, or empty.

cases.draft: fine.
cases.fitWhy: Control correct: a bare 'fine.' is a low-investment reply and the read says so. (Framing note: the verdict speaks of 'they' although the user is sending it; that is the app's receipt-as-read convention.)
cases.intent: Control: a bare 'fine.' genuinely is a low-investment reply. A polite-but-not-invested read fits.

cases.draft: Fine. Do whatever you want.
cases.fitWhy: 'They stayed polite' mislabels a dismissive, contemptuous line; the pattern layer's own label, 'Reluctant agreement', is the truer read and it is buried under the headline.
cases.intent: Same draft, three contexts (e1-e3). On its face this line is dismissive/contemptuous, not polite. Document how the read moves with context and whether the movement is defensible.

cases.draft: Fine. Do whatever you want.
cases.fitWhy: Verdict and confidence are identical to e1; the Rejected feeling changes only advice fields (bestMove 'Create space', 'Do not follow up yet'). Context moving the advice is defensible; context never touching the interpretation is the strain.
cases.intent: Same draft as e1, feeling changed to Rejected. Document what changes and what does not.

cases.draft: Fine. Do whatever you want.
cases.fitWhy: Even under a Conflict scenario with an Annoyed feeling, the verdict never escalates past 'polite, not invested'; the scenario only swaps the suggested stock line. Context rearranges the furniture, not the read.
cases.intent: Same draft as e1, scenario Conflict and feeling Annoyed. Document what changes and what does not.
